summary: Payment failures (60-63% 5xx from 15:00) were caused by ledger-db running out of disk space, NOT by the payment-service v6.0.0 release. The shared Postgres ledger-db filled its /var/lib/postgresql/data volume because an inactive replication slot ('analytics_cdc') retained tens of GB of WAL; disk climbed steadily from 78% at 11:00 to 100% at 15:00, and Postgres began PANICing on WAL/file extension at 15:01. The v6.0.0 deploy (14:46) was only temporally coincident with the final approach to 100%, and rolling it back at 15:12 did not restore service — errors continued at ~62% through 16:48. Root cause category: resource_exhaustion at ledger-db. Remediation: free disk (drop/recover the replication slot, archive/purge WAL, expand volume), then restart ledger-db; the payment-service rollback was misdirected.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from retained WAL (inactive replication slot)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An inactive replication slot ('analytics_cdc') on the shared ledger-db retained tens of GB of WAL, gradually filling /var/lib/postgresql/data from ~78% (11:00) to 100% (~15:00). Postgres could no longer extend files or write WAL, so all ledger writes failed ('No space left on device'), which surfaced as payment-service 5xx for every payment requiring a ledger entry.

causal_chain.claim: Retained WAL fills ledger-db disk to 100%

assumptions: The 'analytics_cdc' slot is the dominant consumer of the growing disk usage (WAL retention is the visible mechanism but disk composition is not directly broken down)
The fault is confined to ledger-db and not a second node

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 deployment introduced a ledger entry-type fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v6.0.0 'new mandate flow / MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type' corrupted or overloaded ledger writes, causing failures that a rollback would fix.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Errors were caused by ledger-db running out of disk ('No space left on device'), disk was already 90% at 13:00 before the 14:46 deploy, the first error (15:00:26) aligns with disk reaching 100% not with the deploy, and the 15:12 rollback did not reduce the error rate (still ~62% at 16:48) — a rollback without recovery contradicts this hypothesis.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service DB connection pool exhaustion
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service exhausted its DB pool, causing write failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~8 connections throughout the incident (F13); the error text is a Postgres disk error, not a pool timeout.

facts.statement: ledger-db disk usage was already at ~90% by 13:00, before the 14:46 v6.0.0 deployment.
Inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' was retaining tens of GB of WAL from at least 12:19:34, well before the deploy.
ledger-db began PANICing and failing file extension with 'No space left on device' at 15:01:01.
First payment-service ledger-write failure was at 15:00:26, aligned with the disk hitting 100%.
Rolling back v6.0.0 at 15:12 did not recover the service: errors continued through 16:57 and error rate stayed ~62% at 16:48.
ledger-db (shared Postgres) is the dependency that failed, and payment-service merely reported the symptom.
payment-service connection pool usage was flat (~8), ruling out pool exhaustion.
A prior incident HIST-114 had the identical signature of ledger-db disk full from retained WAL.

assumptions: WAL retained by the 'analytics_cdc' slot is the dominant contributor to the disk fill; exact disk composition by file type is not directly provided.
The ledger-db change is the only shared component affected; no separate storage/node failure occurred.

timeline.event: First 'analytics_cdc inactive, retaining 63157 MB of WAL' warning

recommended_actions.action: Free space on ledger-db immediately: recover or drop the inactive 'analytics_cdc' replication slot, purge/archive retained WAL, and/or expand the /var/lib/postgresql/data volume; then restart Postgres cleanly.
recommended_actions.rationale: Disk is pinned at 100% and Postgres is PANICing; this is the actual fault. Dropping the inactive slot releases the retained WAL.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the payment-service rollback as the fix; it has not restored service and error rate is unchanged.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback at 15:12 did not reduce errors (still ~62% at 16:48), so it is not the causal fix.

recommended_actions.action: Alert on replication-slot WAL retention and on disk usage thresholds on ledger-db (e.g., page at 85%).
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-114 resolution added a slot-lag alert; the same gap recurred, and disk creeping 78%->100% over hours was only a soft warning.

recommended_actions.action: Add an automated check/monitor that removes or flags abandoned replication slots consuming WAL.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the same failure mode

data_gaps: replication_lag_ms for ledger-db timed out (tc-010) — could not confirm replica/slot lag numbers directly.
api-gateway logs timed out repeatedly (tc-016, tc-017) — upstream 5xx propagation path unverified from the gateway side.
No metric directly attributes disk consumption to WAL vs table growth; the WAL-retention link rests on log warnings plus the historical match.
payment-service request_rate query timed out (tc-015); unable to confirm whether traffic volume also changed.

findings.statement: ledger-db disk usage rose steadily from ~78.6% at 11:00 to 100% by 14:45-15:00 and stayed pinned at 100% through 16:45.
Disk was already ~90% at 13:00, BEFORE the 14:46 v6.0.0 deploy, and there was a disk 90% warning at 13:10:01.
ledger-db repeatedly logged that an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' was retaining tens of GB of WAL, beginning at 12:19:34 — before the deploy.

findings.statement: payment-service error rate jumped from ~0.22% (through 14:48) to 60.85% at 15:00, aligned with the disk filling — not with the 14:46 deploy.
The v6.0.0 deployment (dep-6203, 14:46) was rolled back at 15:12:00.
After the rollback, payment-service errors continued: 320 ERROR ledger-write failures between 15:12 and 16:57 (last at 16:57:54).
payment-service error rate remained ~60-63% after the rollback through 16:48 (no recovery).
ledger-db still logged PANIC/file-extension errors at 15:12-16:58, confirming the disk condition persisted past the rollback.

findings.statement: ledger-db is a shared Postgres datastore used by several services; payment-service writes to it.
payment-service db pool usage stayed flat (~8 connections) throughout, ruling out pool exhaustion as the fault.

A matching historical incident HIST-114 had the same signature: 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL', root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', category resource_exhaustion.
